BIQAI:90:17/r6.claim: Abū Bakr exemplifies this virtue: the author ranks him immediately after the prophets because he displayed these deeds before Islam.
BIQAI:90:17/r6.anchor: ولذلك كان الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه أعلى الناس درجة بعد النبيين

BIQAI:90:17/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:17/r7.speaker: ابن الدغنة
BIQAI:90:17/r7.claim: When Ibn al-Dughunnah found Abū Bakr leaving Mecca after persecution, he praised his kinship, hospitality, care for the burdened, and help in hardship.
BIQAI:90:17/r7.anchor: قال ابن الدغنة حين وجده قد خرج من مكة المشرفة يريد الهجرة

BIQAI:90:17/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:17/r8.speaker: خديجة رضي الله عنها
BIQAI:90:17/r8.claim: The author says Khadīja gave the Prophet the same reassurance and praise when he returned trembling after Gabriel appeared.
BIQAI:90:17/r8.anchor: كما قالت خديجة رضي الله عنها للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين رجع إليها ترجف بوادره من تجلي جبريل

BIQAI:90:17/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:17/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:17/r9.claim: With divine guidance Abū Bakr answered the call immediately, without hesitation, and rose to the highest ranks of Islam.
BIQAI:90:17/r9.anchor: وشرب من صافي مشربه توفيقاً من الله تعالى لم يتلعثم حين دعاه إلى الدين

BIQAI:90:17/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:17/r10.speaker: أبو بكر رضي الله عنه
BIQAI:90:17/r10.claim: At al-Ḥudaybiyya Abū Bakr told ʿUmar what the Prophet had said, word for word, despite not having heard it from him.
BIQAI:90:17/r10.anchor: قال يوم الحديبية لعمر رضي الله عنهما حين أظهر الكراهة للصلح ما قال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سواء حرفاً بحرف

BIQAI:90:17/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:17/r11.speaker: أبو بكر
BIQAI:90:17/r11.claim: Abū Bakr never drank wine; he said he would spend all his wealth on anything that increased his intellect, not on something that removed it.
BIQAI:90:17/r11.anchor: وكان إذا ليم على ذلك في الجاهلية

BIQAI:90:17/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:17/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:17/r12.claim: Praised deeds are valid only with faith: later faith embraces pre-conversion deeds, while deeds after faith plainly depend on it.
BIQAI:90:17/r12.anchor: وتلك الأعمال لا تصح وإن كانت ممدوحة في كل حال إلا بالإيمان

BIQAI:90:17/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:17/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI:90:17/r13.claim: The Prophet said to a convert, “You have accepted Islam with the good you did before.”
BIQAI:90:17/r13.anchor: كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI:90:17/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:17/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:17/r14.claim: Faith raises people from humiliation, moves them to excellent conduct, and leads to the demanding religious laws that oppose natural inclinations.
BIQAI:90:17/r14.anchor: حاملاً له على محاسن الأعمال ومكارم الأفعال

BIQAI:90:17/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:17/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:17/r15.claim: The struggle against one's nature requires courage; because patience is bitter and cannot endure alone, believers encourage each other through acts of obedience and enjoining right.
BIQAI:90:17/r15.anchor: وكان الصبر لمرارته لا يدوم إلا بالتعاون

BIQAI:90:17/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:17/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:17/r16.claim: The required patience reaches from enjoining right through dangerous deeds; courage is proverbial as an hour's patience.
BIQAI:90:17/r16.anchor: فإن الشجاعة كما قيل صبر ساعة

BIQAI:90:17/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:17/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:17/r17.claim: Because conflict can harden people, mercy is a fruit of endurance and justice, a fourth pass that moderates between excess and deficiency.
BIQAI:90:17/r17.anchor: فكانت الرحمة من ثمرات الاصطبار المثمر للعدالة

BIQAI:90:17/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:17/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:17/r18.claim: Repeating the verb “they urged one another” emphasizes how few people practice mercy.
BIQAI:90:17/r18.anchor: مؤكداً بإعادة العامل إشارة إلى قلة العاملين بها

BIQAI:90:17/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:17/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:17/r19.claim: They cultivate great mercy suited to its time and place, orienting themselves toward what brings divine love and aversion for God's sake.
BIQAI:90:17/r19.anchor: الرحمة العظيمة بحسب زمانها ومكانها بأن يوطنوا أنفسهم على كل ما يحمل على الرحمة العظيمة

BIQAI:90:17/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:17/r20.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:17/r20.claim: Before faith they were free of ostentation and self-admiration and ready for purification; faith purified them into full illumination and knowledge.
BIQAI:90:17/r20.anchor: لأنهم كانوا قبل الإيمان خالصين عن الرياء والإعجاب متهيئين للتزكية

DURR:90:17/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:90:17/r1.speaker: هشام بن حسان
DURR:90:17/r1.claim: Hisham explains mutual exhortation to patience as urging one another to observe what God prescribed.
DURR:90:17/r1.anchor: عن هشام بن حسان رضي الله عنه في قوله : { وتواصوا بالصبر } قال : على ما افترض الله .

DURR:90:17/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:90:17/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:90:17/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the mutual exhortation to mercy extends to all people.
DURR:90:17/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما { وتواصوا بالمرحمة } يعني بذلك رحمة الناس كلهم .

IBNASHUR:90:17/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:17/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:17/r1.claim: The clause ثم كان من الذين آمنوا is coordinated with فلا اقتحم العقبة.
IBNASHUR:90:17/r1.anchor: وجملة : { ثم كان من الذين آمنوا } عطف على جملة { فلا اقتحم العقبة }

IBNASHUR:90:17/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:17/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:17/r2.claim: ثم marks rank rather than time: faith is a higher and more fundamental matter in the argument than freeing a captive or feeding someone.
IBNASHUR:90:17/r2.anchor: و { ثم } للتراخي الرتبي فتدل على أن مضمون الجملة المعطوفة بها أرقى رتبة في الغرض المسوق له الكلام

IBNASHUR:90:17/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:17/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:17/r3.claim: The verb كان suggests faith preceded the required good deed; its use in the rebuke implies the criticized person lacked faith.
IBNASHUR:90:17/r3.anchor: وفي فعل { كان } إشعار بأن إيمانه سابق على اقتحام العقبة المطلوبة فيه بطريقة التوبيخ على انتفائها عنه

IBNASHUR:90:17/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:17/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:17/r4.claim: The rebuke implies that good works by a person without faith avail nothing, since faith is the greatest condition for counting deeds.
IBNASHUR:90:17/r4.anchor: وأنه لو فعل شيئاً من هذه الأعمال الحسنة ولم يكن من الذين آمنوا ما نفعه عملُه شيئاً لأنه قد انتفى عنه الحظ الأعظم من الصالحات

IBNASHUR:90:17/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:17/r5.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR:90:17/r5.claim: Aisha asked whether Ibn Judʿan benefited from pre-Islamic kinship care, feeding, freeing captives and slaves, and helping travelers; the Prophet said no, as he never asked forgiveness for his sin on Judgment Day.
IBNASHUR:90:17/r5.anchor: وعن عائشة : أنها قالت : « يا رسول الله إن ابن جدعان كان في الجاهلية يصل الرحم ويطعم الطعام ويفك العاني ويعتق الرقاب

IBNASHUR:90:17/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:17/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:17/r6.claim: By implication, someone who did these good works in the pre-Islamic period and then believed when Islam came would have those works praised.
IBNASHUR:90:17/r6.anchor: ويفهم من الآية بمفهوم صفة الذين آمنوا أنه لو عمل هذه القرب في الجاهلية وآمن بالله حين جاء الإسلام لكان عمله ذلك محموداً

IBNASHUR:90:17/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:17/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:17/r7.claim: Those who take ثم chronologically understand the person to have overcome the obstacle in pre-Islamic times and then accepted Islam afterward.
IBNASHUR:90:17/r7.anchor: ومن يجعل { ثُم } مفيدة للتراخي في الزمان يجعل المعنى : لا اقتحم العقبة واتبعها بالإِيمان

IBNASHUR:90:17/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:17/r8.speaker: حكيم بن حزام
IBNASHUR:90:17/r8.claim: Hakim asked about pre-Islamic charity, emancipation, and kinship; the Prophet replied that he entered Islam with his prior good deeds, which earned reward as though done in Islam.
IBNASHUR:90:17/r8.anchor: حديث حكيم بن حزام في الصحيح : « قال : قلت : يا رسول الله أرأيتَ أشياء كنتُ أتحنث بها في الجاهلية من صدقة أو عتاقة وصلة رحم

IBNASHUR:90:17/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:17/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:17/r9.claim: Calling them members of the community of believers conveys more established faith than simply calling a person a believer; the group description compounds the praise.
IBNASHUR:90:17/r9.anchor: وقال : { من الذين آمنوا } دون أن يقول : ثم كان مؤمناً ، لأن كونه من الذين آمنوا أدل على ثبوت الإِيمان

IBNASHUR:90:17/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:17/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:17/r10.claim: The object of believe is omitted because it is understood as belief in God alone, Muhammad as Messenger, and Islam; the verb is treated as self-sufficient.
IBNASHUR:90:17/r10.anchor: وحُذِف متعلّق { آمنوا } للعلم به أي آمنوا بالله وحده وبرسوله محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ودين الإِسلام

IBNASHUR:90:17/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:17/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:17/r11.claim: Mention of believers prepares the transition to praise of their mutual counsel and the glad tidings that they are the people of the right.

IBNASHUR:90:17/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:17/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:17/r12.claim: Patience is singled out because it underlies every good deed, each of which requires restraining the soul's desires.
IBNASHUR:90:17/r12.anchor: فإن الصبر ملاك الأعمال الصالحة كلها لأنها لا تخلو من كبح الشّهوة النفسانية وذلك من الصبر

IBNASHUR:90:17/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:17/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:17/r13.claim: Mercy is singled out as the foundation of a sound Muslim community, described elsewhere as merciful among themselves.
IBNASHUR:90:17/r13.anchor: والمرحمة ملاك صلاح الجامعة الإسلامية قال تعالى : { رحماء بينهم }

IBNASHUR:90:17/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:17/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:17/r14.claim: Mutually urging mercy also implies that they practice it, since those who exhort others know its value and act on it first.
IBNASHUR:90:17/r14.anchor: والتواصي بالرحمة فضيلة عظيمة ، وهو أيضاً كناية عن اتصافهم بالمرحمة لأن من يوصي بالمرحمة هو الذي عَرَف قدرَها وفضلها

IBNASHUR:90:17/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:17/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:17/r15.claim: The description indirectly exposes polytheists as lacking patience and mercy, a charge made explicit in other passages.
IBNASHUR:90:17/r15.anchor: وفيه تعريض بأن أهل الشرك ليسوا من أهل الصبر ولا من أهل المرحمة ، وقد صُرح بذلك في قوله تعالى

IBNATIYYA:90:17/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:90:17/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:90:17/r1.claim: Then he was among the believers is coordinated with “scaled the obstacle,” carrying the same possible senses of denial, exhortation, or prayer as the earlier phrase.
IBNATIYYA:90:17/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى : [ ثم كان ] معطوف على قوله تعالى : [ اقتحم ] ، ويتوجه فيه معاني ( فلا اقتحم ) المذكورة من النفي والتحضيض والدعاء

IBNATIYYA:90:17/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:90:17/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
IBNATIYYA:90:17/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ prefers the reading fakku raqabah in light of this coordination with “then he was among the believers.”
IBNATIYYA:90:17/r2.anchor: ورجح أبو عمرو بن العلاء قراءته [ فك رقبة ] بقوله تعالى [ ثم كان ]

IBNATIYYA:90:17/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:90:17/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:90:17/r3.claim: Belief belongs to the time of scaling the obstacle, not a later stage: unbelievers could perform the deed, but it would not benefit them.
IBNATIYYA:90:17/r3.anchor: ومعنى [ ثم كان ] أي كان وقت اقتحامه للعقبة

IBNATIYYA:90:17/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:90:17/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:90:17/r4.claim: Mutual counsel to patience means steadfastness in obedience, trials, and divine decree, and restraint from desires and sins.
IBNATIYYA:90:17/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى [ وتواصوا بالصبر ] معناه : على طاعة الله تعالى وبلائه وقضائه ، وعن الشهوات والمعاصي

IBNATIYYA:90:17/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:90:17/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA:90:17/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains marḥama as everything that leads to God’s mercy.
IBNATIYYA:90:17/r5.anchor: و [ المرحمة ] قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : كل ما يؤدي إلى رحمة الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA:90:17/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:90:17/r6.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA:90:17/r6.claim: Others understand marḥama as compassion among people, which sustains human society; without it, people would perish.
IBNATIYYA:90:17/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون : هو التراحم وعطف بعض الناس على بعض ، وفي ذلك قوام الناس ، ولو لم يتراحموا هلكوا

IBNKATHIR:90:17/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:90:17/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:90:17/r1.claim: The person with these pure virtues must also believe in the heart and seek God's reward; Ibn Kathir links this condition to two verses on believing good works.
IBNKATHIR:90:17/r1.anchor: ثم هو مع هذه الأوصاف الجميلة الطاهرة {[30116]} مؤمنٌ بقلبه ، محتسب ثواب ذلك عند الله عز وجل

IBNKATHIR:90:17/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:90:17/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:90:17/r2.claim: Believers who do righteous deeds urge one another to endure people's harm and to show them compassion.
IBNKATHIR:90:17/r2.anchor: أي : كان من المؤمنين العاملين صالحا ، المتواصين بالصبر على أذى الناس ، وعلى الرحمة بهم

IBNKATHIR:90:17/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:90:17/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:90:17/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir cites a hadith saying the Merciful shows mercy to the merciful and urging mercy toward those on earth so those in heaven will show mercy.
IBNKATHIR:90:17/r3.anchor: كما جاء في الحديث :  " الراحمون يرحمهم الرحمن ، ارحموا من في الأرض يرحمكم من في السماء "

IBNKATHIR:90:17/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:90:17/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:90:17/r4.claim: He cites a second hadith: God does not show mercy to one who does not show mercy to people.
IBNKATHIR:90:17/r4.anchor: وفي الحديث الآخر :  " لا يرحم الله من لا يرحم الناس "

IBNKATHIR:90:17/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:90:17/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR:90:17/r5.claim: Abu Dawud transmits from Abdullah ibn Amr that one who does not show mercy to the young and recognize the rights of elders is not one of us.
IBNKATHIR:90:17/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عَمْرو - يرويه - قال :  " من لم يَرْحَم صغيرنا ويَعْرِف حَقَّ كبيرنا ، فليس منا "

KASHSHAF:90:17/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:17/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:90:17/r1.claim: Thumma marks the higher rank and merit of faith after emancipation and charity, not a later time, since faith comes first and righteous deeds do not stand without it.
KASHSHAF:90:17/r1.anchor: جاء بثم لتراخي الإيمان وتباعده في الرتبة والفضيلة عن العتق والصدقة

KASHSHAF:90:17/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:17/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:90:17/r2.claim: Mutual exhortation to patience can mean urging one another to remain steadfast in faith.
KASHSHAF:90:17/r2.anchor: وصى بعضهم بعضا بالصبر على الإيمان والثبات عليه

KASHSHAF:90:17/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:17/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:90:17/r3.claim: Alternatively, patience means restraint from sins, persistence in acts of obedience, and endurance of trials that befall believers.
KASHSHAF:90:17/r3.anchor: أو بالصبر عن المعاصي وعلى الطاعات والمحن التي يبتلى بها المؤمن

KASHSHAF:90:17/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:17/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:90:17/r4.claim: Al-marḥama means mercy: believers exhort each other to compassion and mutual tenderness, or to acts that bring God’s mercy.
KASHSHAF:90:17/r4.anchor: وبأن يكونوا متراحمين متعاطفين . أو بما يؤدي إلى رحمة الله

MAWARDI:90:17/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:17/r1.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI:90:17/r1.claim: Al-Hasan explains mutual exhortation to patience as patience in obeying God.
MAWARDI:90:17/r1.anchor: أحدها : بالصبر على طاعة الله ،   قاله الحسن .

MAWARDI:90:17/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:17/r2.speaker: هشام بن حسان
MAWARDI:90:17/r2.claim: Hisham ibn Hassan says it means patience in fulfilling what God has made obligatory.
MAWARDI:90:17/r2.anchor: الثاني : بالصبر على ما افترض الله عليه ،   قاله هشام بن حسان .

MAWARDI:90:17/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:17/r3.speaker: سفيان
MAWARDI:90:17/r3.claim: Sufyan says it means patience through what has befallen them.
MAWARDI:90:17/r3.anchor: الثالث : بالصبر على ما أصابهم ،   قاله سفيان .

MAWARDI:90:17/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:17/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:90:17/r4.claim: He also suggests patience with worldly life and restraint from its desires.
MAWARDI:90:17/r4.anchor: ويحتمل رابعاً : بالصبر على الدنيا وعن شهواتها .

MAWARDI:90:17/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:17/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI:90:17/r5.claim: Mutual exhortation to mercy means showing compassion among themselves and extending mercy to all people.
MAWARDI:90:17/r5.anchor: { وتَواصَوْا بالمَرْحَمَةِ } أي بالتراحم فيما بينهم ،   فرحموا الناس كلهم .

MAWARDI:90:17/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:17/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI:90:17/r6.claim: Alternatively, mercy means the Hereafter, the abode of mercy, so they urge one another to leave worldly life and seek the next life.
MAWARDI:90:17/r6.anchor: ويحتمل ثانياً : وتواصوا بالآخرة لأنها دار الرحمة ،   فيتواصوا بترك الدنيا وطلب الآخرة .

NASAFI:90:13/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:90:13/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:90:13/r1.claim: He failed to thank God for His blessings through freeing slaves, feeding orphans and the poor, and faith; instead he was ungrateful and denied the Benefactor.
NASAFI:90:13/r1.anchor: يعني فلم يشكر تلك الآيادي والنعم بالأعمال الصالحة من فك الرقاب أو إطعام اليتامى والمساكين ،   ثم بالإيمان

NASAFI:90:13/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:90:13/r14.speaker: author
NASAFI:90:13/r14.claim: Being among the believers means remaining constant in faith.
NASAFI:90:13/r14.anchor: ومعنى { ثُمَّ كَانَ مِنَ الذين ءامَنُواْ } أي داوم على الإيمان

NASAFI:90:13/r15.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:90:13/r15.speaker: author
NASAFI:90:13/r15.claim: One reported explanation takes thumma as equivalent to 'and.'

NASAFI:90:13/r16.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:90:13/r16.speaker: author
NASAFI:90:13/r16.claim: Another explanation gives thumma a delay of rank and merit, not time: faith precedes the deeds and is required for any good deed to stand.
NASAFI:90:13/r16.anchor: وقيل : إنما جاء ب «ثم » لتراخي الإيمان وتباعده في الرتبة والفضيلة عن العتق والصدقة لا في الوقت

NASAFI:90:13/r17.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:90:13/r17.speaker: author
NASAFI:90:13/r17.claim: They urge one another to avoid sins, obey God, and endure the trials through which believers are tested.
NASAFI:90:13/r17.anchor: { وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بالصبر } عن المعاصي وعلى الطاعات والمحن التي يبتلى بها المؤمن

NASAFI:90:13/r18.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:90:13/r18.speaker: author
NASAFI:90:13/r18.claim: They urge one another to show mutual compassion.

NASAFI:90:17/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:90:17/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:90:17/r1.claim: He failed to thank God for His blessings through freeing slaves, feeding orphans and the poor, and faith; instead he was ungrateful and denied the Benefactor.
NASAFI:90:17/r1.anchor: يعني فلم يشكر تلك الآيادي والنعم بالأعمال الصالحة من فك الرقاب أو إطعام اليتامى والمساكين ،   ثم بالإيمان

NASAFI:90:17/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:90:17/r14.speaker: author
NASAFI:90:17/r14.claim: Being among the believers means remaining constant in faith.
NASAFI:90:17/r14.anchor: ومعنى { ثُمَّ كَانَ مِنَ الذين ءامَنُواْ } أي داوم على الإيمان

NASAFI:90:17/r15.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:90:17/r15.speaker: author
NASAFI:90:17/r15.claim: One reported explanation takes thumma as equivalent to 'and.'

NASAFI:90:17/r16.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:90:17/r16.speaker: author
NASAFI:90:17/r16.claim: Another explanation gives thumma a delay of rank and merit, not time: faith precedes the deeds and is required for any good deed to stand.
NASAFI:90:17/r16.anchor: وقيل : إنما جاء ب «ثم » لتراخي الإيمان وتباعده في الرتبة والفضيلة عن العتق والصدقة لا في الوقت

NASAFI:90:17/r17.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:90:17/r17.speaker: author
NASAFI:90:17/r17.claim: They urge one another to avoid sins, obey God, and endure the trials through which believers are tested.
NASAFI:90:17/r17.anchor: { وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بالصبر } عن المعاصي وعلى الطاعات والمحن التي يبتلى بها المؤمن

NASAFI:90:17/r18.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:90:17/r18.speaker: author
NASAFI:90:17/r18.claim: They urge one another to show mutual compassion.

QURTUBI:90:17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:17/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:90:17/r1.claim: A person cannot pass the obstacle by freeing a slave or feeding the hungry unless he is among those who believe; faith is a condition for deeds to be accepted and must accompany them.
QURTUBI:90:17/r1.anchor: حتى يكون من الذين آمنوا ،   أي صدقوا ،   فإن شرط قبول الطاعات الإيمان بالله .

QURTUBI:90:17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:17/r2.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI:90:17/r2.claim: Aisha asks about Ibn Jud‘an, who aided relatives and the needy in pre-Islamic times; the Prophet says it will not benefit him because he never asked forgiveness for Judgment Day.
QURTUBI:90:17/r2.anchor: وقالت عائشة : يا رسول الله ،   إن ابن جدعان كان في الجاهلية يصل الرحم ،   ويطعم الطعام

QURTUBI:90:17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:17/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:90:17/r3.claim: One view is that he performed these good deeds as a believer and remained faithful until death, as in the command to repent, believe, act well, then remain guided.
QURTUBI:90:17/r3.anchor: وقيل :  " ثم كان من الذين آمنوا "  أي فعل هذه الأشياء وهو مؤمن ،   ثم بقي على إيمانه حتى الوفاة

QURTUBI:90:17/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:17/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:90:17/r4.claim: Another view takes the phrase to mean believing that such deeds will benefit one before God.
QURTUBI:90:17/r4.anchor: وقيل : المعنى ثم كان من الذين يؤمنون بأن هذا نافع لهم عند الله تعالى .

QURTUBI:90:17/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:17/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:90:17/r5.claim: Another view says he first performed these charitable acts for God and then believed in Muhammad.
QURTUBI:90:17/r5.anchor: وقيل : أتى بهذه القرب لوجه الله ،   ثم آمن بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم .

QURTUBI:90:17/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:17/r6.speaker: حكيم بن حزام
QURTUBI:90:17/r6.claim: After converting, Hakim ibn Hizam asks whether good deeds from the pre-Islamic period count; the Prophet replies that he entered Islam bringing the good he had already done.
QURTUBI:90:17/r6.anchor: وقد قال حكيم بن حزام بعدما أسلم ،   يا رسول الله ،   إنا كنا نتحنث{[16085]} بأعمال في الجاهلية

QURTUBI:90:17/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:17/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:90:17/r7.claim: A grammatical view takes ثم as equivalent to waw, meaning the person who freed a slave or fed the hungry was among the believers.

QURTUBI:90:17/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:17/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI:90:17/r8.claim: Tawāṣaw means that they advised one another.
QURTUBI:90:17/r8.anchor: وتواصوا "  أي أوصى بعضهم بعضا .    " بالصبر "

QURTUBI:90:17/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:17/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI:90:17/r9.claim: Patience means steadfastness in obeying God, refraining from disobedience, and enduring trials and calamities.
QURTUBI:90:17/r9.anchor: " بالصبر "  أي بالصبر على طاعة الله ،   وعن معاصيه ،   وعلى ما أصابهم من البلاء

QURTUBI:90:17/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:17/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI:90:17/r10.claim: Mercy means showing compassion to creation, which leads people to care for orphans and the poor.
QURTUBI:90:17/r10.anchor: " وتواصوا بالمرحمة "  بالرحمة على الخلق ،   فإنهم إذا فعلوا ذلك رحموا اليتيم والمسكين .

RAZI:90:17/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:17/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:90:17/r1.claim: The one who overcomes the obstacle must be among the believers; without faith the acts of obedience bring no benefit and do not constitute a successful crossing.
RAZI:90:17/r1.anchor: فإنه إن لم يكن منهم لم ينتفع بشيء من هذه الطاعات ، ولا مقتحما للعقبة

RAZI:90:17/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:17/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:90:17/r2.claim: One explanation is that ثم delays the mention of faith, not its existence; the cited verse means to mention the father's prior eminence afterward.
RAZI:90:17/r2.anchor: أن هذا التراخي في الذكر لا في الوجود ، كقوله

RAZI:90:17/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:17/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:90:17/r3.claim: A line illustrates that ثم can order mention rather than events: the father and grandfather had already attained eminence before the person named first.
RAZI:90:17/r3.anchor: إن من ساد ثم ساد أبوه *** ثم قد ساد قبل ذلك جده

RAZI:90:17/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:17/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:90:17/r4.claim: A second explanation places faith at the end of the person's life: dying in faith is a condition for receiving the benefit of deeds.
RAZI:90:17/r4.anchor: أن يكون المراد ، ثم كان في عاقبة أمره من الذين آمنوا

RAZI:90:17/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:17/r5.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI:90:17/r5.claim: Some hold that deeds done devotionally before belief in Muhammad can still be rewarded if their doer later believes in him.
RAZI:90:17/r5.anchor: فعند بعضهم أنه يثاب على تلك الطاعات

RAZI:90:17/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:17/r6.speaker: حكيم بن حزام
RAZI:90:17/r6.claim: Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām asked the Prophet about good deeds from the pre-Islamic period, and the Prophet replied that he had embraced Islam with the good he had already done.
RAZI:90:17/r6.anchor: أن حكيم بن حزام بعدما أسلم قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «إنا كنا نأتي بأعمال الخير في الجاهلية

RAZI:90:17/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:17/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:90:17/r7.claim: A fourth explanation takes ثم as ranking faith later in merit: its reward far exceeds the reward for the other deeds.
RAZI:90:17/r7.anchor: تراخي الإيمان وتباعده في الرتبة والفضيلة عن العنق والصدقة لأن درجة ثواب الإيمان أعظم بكثير

RAZI:90:17/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:17/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:90:17/r8.claim: Exhorting one another to patience includes steadfastness in faith, restraint from sins, perseverance in worship, and endurance of believers' trials.
RAZI:90:17/r8.anchor: يوصي بعضهم بعضا بالصبر على الإيمان والثبات عليه أو الصبر على المعاصي وعلى الطاعات والمحن

RAZI:90:17/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:17/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:90:17/r9.claim: Mutual exhortation to mercy means urging compassion for the oppressed and poor, and restraining someone approaching a wrongdoing.
RAZI:90:17/r9.anchor: أن يحث بعضهم بعضا على أن يرحم المظلوم أو الفقير ، أو يرحم المقدم على منكر فيمنعه منه

RAZI:90:17/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:17/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:90:17/r10.claim: The verse indicates that a person must guide others toward truth and, as far as possible, stop them from following evil and falsehood.
RAZI:90:17/r10.anchor: وهذا يدل على أنه يجب على المرء أن يدل غيره على طريق الحق ويمنعه من سلوك طريق الشر والباطل

RAZI:90:17/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:17/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:90:17/r11.claim: Those described as overcoming the obstacle are the foremost Companions, including the four caliphs, known for steadfastness in religion and mercy toward people.

RAZI:90:17/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:17/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:90:17/r12.claim: Patience expresses honoring God's command, while mercy expresses compassion for God's creatures; together they encompass the foundations of obedience.

RAZI:90:17/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:17/r13.speaker: بعض المحققين
RAZI:90:17/r13.claim: Some investigators describe the foundations of Sufism as sincerity with God and good character with people.
RAZI:90:17/r13.anchor: إن الأصل في التصوف أمران : صدق مع الحق ؟ وخلق مع الخلق

ITQAN:v3p74/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p74/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p74/r4.claim: One proposed resolution takes ثم as equivalent to واو, so there is no difficulty.
ITQAN:v3p74/r4.anchor: أما الثالث ففيه أجوبة أخرى منها أن ﴿ ثم ﴾ بمعنى الواو فلا إيراد

ITQAN:v3p74/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p74/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p74/r5.claim: Another view says ثم orders the statement or report, not the event reported; 90:17 is cited as an example.
ITQAN:v3p74/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد ترتيب الخبر لا المخبر به كقوله ﴿ ثم كان من الذين آمنوا ﴾

ITQAN:v3p74/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p74/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p74/r6.claim: A further view retains the ordinary sequential sense of ثم, but applies it to the relation between the two creations rather than to elapsed time.
ITQAN:v3p74/r6.anchor: وقيل على بابها وهي لتعارف ما بين الخلقين لا للتراخي في الزمان

ITQAN:v3p74/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p74/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p74/r7.claim: Another proposed answer understands خلق to mean قدر, that is, to decree or determine.

ITQAN:v3p74/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p74/r8.speaker: الشمس الكرماني
ITQAN:v3p74/r8.claim: Al-Shams al-Kirmani explains that God's naming as forgiving and merciful is past in its relation, while the divine attributes persist and take effect whenever He wills forgiveness or mercy.
ITQAN:v3p74/r8.anchor: وأما الصفتان فلا تزالان كذلك لا ينقطعان لأنه تعالى إذا أراد المغفرة أو الرحمة في الحال أو الاستقبال وقع مراده قاله الشمس الكرماني

ITQAN:v3p74/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p74/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v3p74/r9.claim: A possible second answer from Ibn Abbas takes كان to mean permanence: God continues to be so.
ITQAN:v3p74/r9.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ابن عباس أجاب بجوابين أحدهما أن التسمية هي التي كانت وانتهت والصفة لا نهاية لها والآخر أن معنى ( كان ) الدوام

ITQAN:v3p74/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p74/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p74/r10.claim: The question may read the wording as implying either that God was merciful before anyone needed mercy, or that He is not merciful now because كان is past tense.
ITQAN:v3p74/r10.anchor: ويحتمل أن يحمل السؤال على مسلكين والجواب على دفعهما كأن يقال هذا اللفظ مشعر بأنه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p204/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p204/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p204/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes ثم to mark faith's higher rank and distance in merit from freeing a slave or feeding the needy, not later timing, since faith must precede valid deeds.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p204/r1.anchor: ونص عبارة "الزمخشري" في (الكشاف) : "جاء بـ (ثم) لتراخي الإيمان وتباعده في الفضيلة والرتبة عن العتق والصدقة، لا في الوقت.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p204/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p204/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p204/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan offers three readings: delay in rank, the person's eventual death among believers, or delay in the order of mention; he too denies temporal delay for the first reading.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p204/r2.anchor: وإلى مثل هذا ذهب "أبو حيان" وزاده تفصيلاً فقال: "ثم: لتراخي الإيمان في الفضيلة لا للتراخي في الزمان

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p204/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p204/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p204/r3.claim: She rejects these adjustments and reads ثم in its plain contextual sequence: emancipation and compassion are prior steps required for faith, which is absent from the enslaver and the callous person who neglects the hungry orphan or poor.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p204/r3.anchor: نأخذ حرف "ثم" على صريح معناه في السياق، فنفهم أن القرآن إذ يرتب مراحل اقتحام العقبة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p204/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p204/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p204/r4.claim: She links this reading to al-Ma'un, where denial of the Judgment is manifested in pushing away the orphan and failing to urge feeding the poor.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p204/r4.anchor: ويؤنس إلى هذا الفهم لحرف "ثم" آية الماعون

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p203/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p203/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p203/r3.claim: Commentators strained the plain sequence in which faith follows freeing a slave because ثم marks order with delay, interpreting beyond the passage's apparent sense.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p203/r3.anchor: عطف الإيمان على فك رقبة، بحرف "ثم" الذي يفيد الترتيب مع التراخي
